bib.title: Jukebox: A Generative Model for Music

read.skipped: reference list and t-SNE artist-name lists skimmed

question: Can a single model generate diverse, high-fidelity music with singing in the raw audio domain with coherence over minutes?
hypothesis: Compressing raw audio with a multi-scale VQ-VAE and modelling the discrete codes with autoregressive Transformers at scale makes long raw-audio music generation feasible.
contributions: Multi-scale VQ-VAE with random restarts, separate autoencoders and a spectral loss
Scalable Transformer priors and upsamplers over discrete codes
Conditioning on artist, genre, timing and unaligned lyrics
Release of weights, code and samples

method.summary: Three separate VQ-VAEs compress 44.1 kHz audio by 8x, 32x and 128x. A 5B top-level prior and two 1B upsamplers model the codes autoregressively with sparse (axis-aligned) Transformers, conditioned on artist, genre, timing and lyrics. Sampling is ancestral top to bottom, with windowed and primed variants.
method.task: raw-audio music generation (VQ-VAE codes + autoregressive priors)

datasets.name: scraped song dataset (LyricWiki lyrics/metadata)
datasets.source: scraped; lyrics and metadata from LyricWiki
datasets.preprocessing: 32 bit 44.1 kHz audio; random downmix of left/right to mono as augmentation; later restricted to primarily-English songs; 24 sec chunks with lyric windows aligned via Spleeter + NUS AutoLyricsAlign

datasets.name: MAESTRO
datasets.source: first model only, 22 kHz VQ-VAE codes

models.name: Music VQ-VAE (3 levels)
models.architecture: non-causal dilated 1-D conv residual encoder/decoder, EMA codebook

models.name: Top-level prior
models.architecture: Scalable Transformer; lyrics encoder + 7 encoder-decoder attention layers
models.init_from: lyrics model reuses pretrained unconditional top-level prior as decoder, new layers zero-init

training.objective: VQ-VAE: L_recons + L_codebook + beta*L_commit + multi-STFT spectral loss; priors/upsamplers: next-token maximum likelihood
training.lr: 0.00015 for 5B prior (Table 6); 0.0003 for VQ-VAE and upsamplers
training.precision: fully half precision (weights, gradients, Adam state) with dynamic scaling
training.hardware: V100 GPUs (VQ-VAE 256; upsamplers 128; top prior 512; lyrics 512)
training.compute: VQ-VAE 3 days on 256 V100; upsamplers 2 weeks on 128 V100; 5B prior 4 weeks on 512 V100; lyrics model 2 weeks on 512 V100

inference.decoding: ancestral sampling top to bottom; windowed sampling advances by half the context; primed sampling from 12 s of real audio
inference.samples: full tree: 4 independent samples per one-minute extension, 16 completions at 3 min; no further counts
inference.prompting: artist, genre, timing and lyrics conditioning

other.speed: about an hour to generate 1 minute of top level tokens; about 8 hours to upsample one minute

metrics.name: spectral convergence
metrics.definition: spectral error relative to signal for VQ-VAE reconstruction

baselines: Opus codec at comparable bitrate (qualitative, Fig 4)
eval.protocol: VQ-VAE: 5000 held-out 3-second segments, average in dB. Generation: manual listening for coherence, musicality, diversity, novelty; no MOS or FID.

results.claim: The 5B top-level prior takes about an hour to generate one minute of top-level tokens.
results.unit: hour per minute of top-level tokens
results.quote: The current model takes around an hour to generate 1 minute

results.claim: Upsampling one minute of top-level tokens takes about 8 hours because it is sequential.
results.quote: it takes around 8 hours to upsample one minute of top level tokens

results.claim: The authors state the asymmetry: fast parallel likelihood evaluation, slow autoregressive sampling.
results.quote: Our models have fast parallel evaluation of likelihood but slow autoregressive sampling.

results.claim: Reconstruction error rises with hop length; bottom level with restarts reaches -23.0 dB, top level -8.3 dB.
results.table: Table 1, rows Bottom/Middle/Top, column With restart

results.claim: Reducing codebook size from 2048 to 256 worsens bottom-level reconstruction from -23.0 to -15.9 dB.
Top-level reconstruction degrades without spectral loss (-6.3 dB) and with a single hierarchical autoencoder (2.9 dB), versus -8.3 dB.
results.table: Table 3, rows Without spectral loss, With single autoencoder

results.claim: Context of 8192 tokens spans about 24, 6 and 1.5 seconds of audio at top, middle and bottom level.
results.quote: which corresponds to approximately 24, 6, and 1.5 seconds

results.claim: Samples stay coherent through the top-level context (about 24 s) but lack long-term structure such as repeated choruses.

limits: Evaluation is manual listening; authors say MOS or FID-like metrics are not meaningful
No repeated choruses or long-term structure; noise or scratchiness at small scale
